title: World Bosses
content: World bosses are raid-level creatures in the shared outdoor world, so guilds may compete for their respawns. Vanilla examples include Lord Kazzak in the Blasted Lands, Azuregos in Azshara, and the green dragons Emeriss, Lethon, Taerar, and Ysondre at dream portals. They require a coordinated raid, can punish deaths or poor positioning, and drop rare epic loot. Doom Lord Kazzak is a later Outland encounter and is not part of this ruleset.

title: Rare Elite Creatures
content: Rare and rare-elite creatures spawn less often than normal enemies and may patrol or use unusual abilities. Vanilla examples include Prince Nazjak in Arathi Highlands, Broken Tooth in the Badlands, and many silver-dragon beasts valued by hunters. They can drop uncommon equipment or sought-after pets, but Vanilla has no achievement reward simply for killing every rare. Respawn times vary and custom Turtle WoW zones add their own rares.

title: Important Quest Givers
content: Quest givers marked by an available quest can begin local stories, class chains, attunements, and reputation work. Important Vanilla figures such as Thrall, King Magni Bronzebeard, Tirion Fordring, Eitrigg, and Duke Hydraxis participate in notable chains. Read dialogue and completion text because objectives can span several zones, require prerequisites, or unlock follow-up quests that are not visible until the current step is finished.

title: Class and Profession Trainers
content: Class trainers teach new ability ranks as players level, while class trainers also reset talents for an increasing gold cost. Profession trainers teach skill ranks and recipes, although Artisan ranks, specializations, and rare recipes may require a particular trainer, book, vendor, drop, or quest. Visit a suitable capital or class hub periodically because trained abilities are not granted automatically.

title: Special Vendors
content: Special vendors sell unique items not available elsewhere. Examples include the Argent Dawn vendors (for Stratholme), the Thorium Brotherhood vendors (for Blackrock Depths), or the Darkmoon Faire vendors. Some vendors require reputation or special currencies. Finding and accessing special vendors is part of efficient gearing strategies.

title: Flight Masters
content: Flight masters provide taxi travel by gryphon, hippogryph, wyvern, bat, or custom route. Speak to a flight master to learn that node before it can be used, then pay for a connected route. Not every zone has a node and opposite-faction routes remain separate. Turtle WoW adds flight points for custom settlements, so visiting new hubs is important even when a Vanilla route is already familiar.

title: Innkeepers and Hearthstones
content: Innkeepers let a character bind the Hearthstone to that inn and place the character in a rested area. A Hearthstone returns to the bound location after its cooldown, so rebinding near an active quest hub can save substantial travel. Capitals also grant rest. Inns use the same rested rules; nearby mailboxes, vendors, or transport links simply make some locations more convenient than others.

title: Bankers and Guild Banks
content: Bankers in major cities open personal bank storage, whose bag slots can be expanded by purchasing bank-bag slots. This TortoiseWoW core also contains a custom guild-bank system with shared storage controlled by guild rank permissions when the server enables it. Keep valuable materials organized, verify withdrawal rights before relying on shared stock, and use mail or bank alts when personal space is limited.

title: Auctioneers
content: Auctioneers manage the auction house where players can buy and sell items. They are located in major cities. Auctioneers handle posting auctions, bidding, and collecting winnings. Understanding how to use the auction house effectively is crucial for the in-game economy. Different cities have different auction houses with varying activity levels.

title: Stable Masters
content: Stable masters manage hunter combat pets, not mounts. Hunters can place an active pet in a purchased stable slot, retrieve a stored pet, or make room to tame a beast whose abilities they want to learn. Pet loyalty, happiness, food family, and trained abilities still matter. Vanilla mounts are normally learned or carried through their own mount system and are not stored by a stable master.

title: Important Lore Figures
content: Important figures in the Vanilla-plus timeline include Thrall, Cairne Bloodhoof, Sylvanas Windrunner, Tyrande Whisperwind, Malfurion Stormrage, Jaina Proudmoore, Bolvar Fordragon, Tirion Fordring, and echoes of figures such as Medivh. Their dialogue and quest chains explain faction politics, the Scourge, the Burning Legion, ancient conflicts, and Turtle WoW's custom stories. A lore figure may be a ruler, quest giver, raid participant, or historical character rather than a normal combat target.

title: Faction Leaders
content: Vanilla-era faction leaders include Thrall in Orgrimmar, Cairne Bloodhoof in Thunder Bluff, Sylvanas Windrunner in Undercity, Tyrande Whisperwind in Darnassus, and King Magni Bronzebeard in Ironforge. Stormwind is governed for the young King Anduin through Regent Lord Bolvar Fordragon in this timeline. Turtle WoW's High Elves and Goblins add their own leaders and settlements. Leaders can anchor quests and city defense but should not be replaced with later-expansion rulers.

title: Specialized Merchants
content: Specialized merchants sell specific types of goods. Weapon merchants, armorers, reagent vendors, poison vendors. Some merchants are only available in certain locations or require special access. Finding the right merchants is important for gearing up and obtaining necessary supplies. Different merchants offer different quality and selection of goods.

title: City Guards and Sentries
content: Guards protect cities and provide security. They attack hostile players and creatures. Guards have different levels and abilities based on the city. Some guards provide directions or information. Guards help maintain order in cities and make them safe for players. Different races have different guard appearances and behaviors.

title: Transportation NPCs
content: Boats, zeppelins, the Deeprun Tram, flight masters, and custom Turtle WoW routes connect distant regions. Examples include zeppelins serving Orgrimmar and Undercity, the Booty Bay-Ratchet boat, and the tram between Stormwind and Ironforge. Crews and platform NPCs can indicate a route, but departures run on schedules and usually need no ticket. Mages provide player-made teleports and portals rather than a normal transport NPC service.
